Admittedly, wasn't easy to figure out as a new person too. 

The way it was initially explained to me is that one good method isn't to just impromptu bang out an EIP (unless you're Wilford of course 🙂 ), it's to engage in discussions about what the issue to fix or change is first. Once that occurs for how much ever time and discussion is needed there will better footing for a cleaner and more understandable EIP proposal. 

Then you can fork EIP git repo, follow EIP-1 as a guide, and do a pull request. 
<https://github.com/ergoplatform/eips>

The idea was, if a new non dev comes into chat and discusses some changes that warrant an EIP, by the end of the discussions they should have enough help/assistance to be able to fork and update. 

My initial thought would be, beyond how easy it is to manage this on github, having another system might take a LOT more oversight and work. Cardano does it here nicely but im sure with a decent amount of commitment: <https://cips.cardano.org/>
